Yeditepe University Eye Center in Beşiktaş, on the European side of Istanbul, opened on 17 January 2007 on 2,250 m². As part of Yeditepe University Hospitals it diagnoses and treats eye diseases in 15 specialist areas and trains eye specialists.

About the centre

The centre is in the Balmumcu district, close to Barbaros Boulevard and Büyükdere Avenue.

Yeditepe University Koşuyolu Hospital in Kadıköy, on the Asian side of Istanbul, has 180 beds, six intensive care beds and nine operating theatres on 35,000 m² of indoor space. Around 100 specialists and academic physicians work at the hospital.

About the hospital

The hospital focuses on neurosciences and oncology: neurosurgery, cancer surgery, medical oncology, bone marrow transplantation for children and adults, orthopaedics, thoracic surgery, ENT, general surgery, gastroenterology, nuclear medicine and interventional radiology.

An intraoperative 3 Tesla MRI scanner is installed in the neurosurgical operating theatre. As part of infection prevention, the surfaces of the hospital were treated with a boron-based antimicrobial coating developed at Yeditepe University.

Koşuyolu Hospital holds the JCI accreditation as an Academic Medical Center (valid until 2028).

Yeditepe University Kozyatağı Hospital in Ataşehir, on the Asian side of Istanbul, opened on 26 August 2005. It has 190 beds and a wide range of departments, from internal medicine and cardiology to obstetrics, IVF and paediatrics.

About the hospital

The building was planned with fire-resistant, scratch-resistant and antibacterial materials. Particular attention is paid to hygiene and sterilisation: in addition to manual disinfection, all patient beds can be cleaned with a high-temperature water spray system.

The imaging centre is equipped with multislice computed tomography (CT) and 3 Tesla magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
